skill.name: entra-agent-id
skill.description: Provision Microsoft Entra Agent Identity Blueprints, principals, and per-instance identities. Configure Microsoft Graph permissions, OAuth token exchange, OBO, federation, and the AgentID sidecar.
skill.summary: Build and secure Microsoft Entra identities and OAuth flows for AI agent instances.
skill.author: microsoft

security_audit.summary: Most static alerts are false positives caused by Markdown syntax, OAuth scope strings, official Microsoft endpoints, and bounded configuration examples. One example can forward an agent bearer token to an unrestricted URL, while semantic review found an exposed sidecar port and broad long-lived delegated grants.

remediation.issue: A helper forwards an agent bearer token to any endpoint parameter.
remediation.suggestion: Require HTTPS and allowlist trusted downstream origins before attaching the Authorization header. Reject redirects to unapproved hosts.

remediation.issue: The Docker Compose example publishes the authentication sidecar on all host interfaces.
remediation.suggestion: Remove the host port mapping or bind it to 127.0.0.1. Keep unauthenticated token endpoints on a private container network.

remediation.issue: Delegated permission examples use AllPrincipals, broad scopes, and a ten-year expiry.
remediation.suggestion: Use the smallest required scopes, shorten grant duration, document approval, and review each Agent Identity grant regularly.

content.value_statement: Agent identity provisioning and OAuth token exchange require coordinated Microsoft Graph configuration. This skill provides workflows for Blueprints, per-instance identities, permissions, and sidecar deployment.
actual_capabilities: Creates Agent Identity Blueprints, BlueprintPrincipals, and per-instance Agent Identities through Microsoft Graph.
Explains application and delegated permission grants for individual Agent Identities.
Builds two-step fmi_path token exchanges for autonomous and on-behalf-of flows.
Configures managed identity federation and development client secrets on Blueprints.
Documents cross-tenant token exchange requirements and common Entra error codes.
Provides Docker, Kubernetes, Python, and TypeScript patterns for the AgentID sidecar.
limitations: Requires appropriate Microsoft Entra roles, Graph permissions, and administrator consent.
Microsoft Graph Agent ID APIs can change during preview and require documentation verification.
Client secrets are suitable only for local development; production requires federated or managed identity.
The skill does not replace standard app registration, Azure RBAC, or agent authoring tools.

use_cases.title: Provision an agent identity hierarchy
use_cases.description: Create a Blueprint, its principal, and separately auditable identities for each deployed agent instance.

use_cases.title: Implement runtime token exchange
use_cases.description: Configure autonomous or on-behalf-of authentication with per-agent Microsoft Graph permissions.

use_cases.title: Deploy a polyglot authentication sidecar
use_cases.description: Prepare local Docker or Kubernetes sidecar configuration for agents written in any supported language.

prompt_templates.title: Check prerequisites
prompt_templates.prompt: List the Entra roles, Graph permissions, tools, and tenant details required to create an Agent Identity Blueprint. Do not make changes.

prompt_templates.title: Plan identity provisioning
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a step-by-step plan for a Blueprint named {name} with {count} Agent Identities. Include sponsors, permissions, validation, and rollback.

prompt_templates.title: Design an OBO flow
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an on-behalf-of flow for {agent} using {scopes}. Explain Blueprint API configuration, per-agent grants, token audiences, and validation.

prompt_templates.title: Review a production deployment
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my AgentID sidecar and cross-tenant token design. Identify excessive permissions, exposed endpoints, credential risks, tenant mistakes, and concrete remediations.

output_examples.input: Plan three identities for a customer-support agent with read-only user access.
output: Prerequisites: required Entra role, Graph permissions, sponsor user, and tenant identifiers.
Sequence: create Blueprint, create BlueprintPrincipal, create three named Agent Identities, then verify each object.
Permission plan: grant only the approved read-only role to each identity and record object identifiers.

output_examples.input: Explain why my autonomous token exchange returns AADSTS82001.
output_examples.output: The flow used the RFC 8693 token-exchange grant. Use client credentials with fmi_path, then request the Graph default scope in step two.

output_examples.input: Review a Kubernetes AgentID sidecar deployment.
output: Keep the sidecar bound to loopback and avoid LoadBalancer or Ingress exposure.
Use workload identity with a signed assertion file instead of a client secret.
Separate non-secret configuration from credentials and apply resource limits and health probes.

best_practices: Verify current Microsoft documentation before applying Graph request bodies or SDK configuration.
Use workload identity federation in production and keep sidecar endpoints private.
Grant the minimum permissions to each Agent Identity and confirm propagation before testing.
anti_patterns: Do not attach credentials directly to Agent Identity service principals.
Do not expose AgentID sidecar token endpoints through public ports, ingress, or load balancers.
Do not grant broad Microsoft Graph scopes when a smaller per-agent permission set works.

faq.question: What objects does this skill create?
faq.answer: It covers an Agent Identity Blueprint, its BlueprintPrincipal, and separate Agent Identity service principals for individual instances.

faq.question: Can I use DefaultAzureCredential?
faq.answer: No. The documented Agent Identity APIs reject Azure CLI tokens carrying Directory.AccessAsUser.All. Use dedicated application or delegated credentials.

faq.question: Where should credentials be stored?
faq.answer: Store credentials on the Blueprint. Use workload identity federation or managed identity for production and client secrets only for development.

faq.question: Does the skill support on-behalf-of authentication?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains Blueprint API configuration, user token audiences, delegated grants, and the two-step OBO exchange.

faq.question: Can the sidecar be publicly exposed?
faq.answer: No. Keep it on loopback or a private container network because some token acquisition endpoints do not require inbound authentication.

faq.question: Does this replace standard Entra app registration guidance?
faq.answer: No. It is specific to Microsoft Entra Agent ID objects and related token flows.
